Spontaneous Communications: The public is encouraged to address the Senior Citizen Commission on any matter listed on the agenda
or on any other matter within its jurisdiction. The Senior Citizen Commission will hear public comments on items listed on the agenda
during discussion of the matter and prior to a vote. The Senior Citizen Commission will hear public comments on matters not listed

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain
emergency or special circumstances exist. The Senior Citizen Commission may request from staff to investigate and/or schedule
certain matters for consideration at a future Commission or City Council meeting.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a Commission meeting or
other services offered by this City, please contact City Hall at (626) 430-2200. Assisted listening devices are available at this meeting.
Ask the Deputy City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and documents in the agenda packet can be made

the meeting or service.

  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Senior Citizen Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are committed
to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter and spirit of
Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private life. We will
be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality and
integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain from
abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which we
have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create a
perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest in
thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

  SPONTANEOUS COMMUNICATIONS
This is the time set aside for members of the audience to speak on items not on this agenda. State law prohibits any
Commission discussion or action on such communications unless 1) the Commission by majority vote finds that a
catastrophe or emergency exists; or 2) the Commission by at least four votes finds that the matter (and need for action
thereon) arose within the last five days. Since the Commission cannot (except as stated) participate it is requested that
all such communications be made in writing so as to be included on the next agenda for full discussion and action. If a
member of the audience feels he or she must proceed tonight, then each speaker will be limited to 2 minutes and each
subject limited to 6 minutes, unless such time limits are extended.

In the hybrid format, both in-person and hybrid audience members will participate in the following order:

  Tier 1: In-person attendees

  Tier 2: Teleconference attendees

  Tier 3: In-person attendees who have not previously provided comments on the matter(s) being
  discussed by the legislative body

  Tier 4: Teleconference attendees who have not previously provided comments on the matter(s) being discussed
  by the legislative body

 IRWINDALE COUNCIL CHAMBER  AUGUST 22, 2022
5050 N. IRWINDALE AVENUE  MONDAY
IRWINDALE, CALIFORNIA 91706  9:00 A.M.

The Irwindale SENIOR CITIZEN COMMISSION met in regular session at the above time and place.

ROLL CALL:  Present: Commissioners Carol Acosta, Patricia Gonzales,
  Iris Rodriguez; Vice Chair Maggie Guzman; Chair Virginia Diaz

  Also present: Elizabeth Rodriguez, Public Services Director;
  Eloise Beltran, Senior Center Manager; Jeff Wagner, IT Manager; and
  Armando Hegdahl, Management Analyst

SPONTANEOUS
COMMUNICATIONS  There were no speakers.

CONSENT CALENDAR

MOTION  A motion was made by Commissioner Gonzales, seconded by
  Commissioner Rodriguez, to approve the Consent Calendar. The
  motion was unanimously approved.

ITEM NO. 1A  MINUTES
MINUTES
  The minutes of the regular meeting held July 25, 2022, were
  approved.

END OF CONSENT CALENDAR

NEW BUSINESS  None.

SENIOR CENTER
MANAGER UPDATE  Manager Beltran provided the following update:

  1) The following events and activities have been scheduled:
  A) The Summer Western Dance held last Friday was sold out and
  enjoyed by all.
  B) The Intergenerational Activity event held last Wednesday had
  participating seniors make five quilts, to be donated to a
  worthwhile organization such as Children’s Hospital or Cory’s
  Kitchen.
  C) This week’s activity in the “Six-Week Challenge” will include
  chair volleyball. The program will end next week with a senior
  trivia. A drawing will be held on August 31 to determine which
  program participant will win the Fitbit.
  D) Residents can begin registering for the Mexican Independence
  Day Dance, which is scheduled for September 16.
  E) The Birthday Breakfast event will be held this Friday.
  F) A Parking Lot Sale will be held on September 24. Nine vendors
  have already signed up. Pozole will be sold as part of a
  fundraiser during the event.
 SENIOR CITIZEN COMMISSION MINUTES  AUGUST 22, 2022
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 2

  G) A field trip to the Aquarium of the Pacific, which was held last
  week, was enjoyed by all.
  H) A field trip to Harrah’s Casino has been scheduled for
  September 17.
  I) All Irwindale classes are off this week; all Mt. Sac classes, with
  the exception of Chair Yoga, will begin this week.
  J) Android phone and iPhone workshops will be held in September.
  K) The Senior Center held two fundraisers recently: one during the
  “Red, White, and You” event, which was not very successful, and
  another during a Music in the Park concert, which was much
  more successful.

CHAIR DIAZ  Responding to a question by Chair Diaz, Manager Beltran advised that
  three children participated in the recent Intergenerational Activity.

VICE CHAIR GUZMAN  Vice Chair Guzman asked why potluck are disallowed at the Senior
  Center, to which Manager Beltran indicated that they are not permitted
  due to COVID-19 recommendations. However, staff will follow-up on
  tine inquiry to determine whether it is permissible now.

  Vice Chair Guzman thanked the Police Department staff for checking on
  resident seniors during the recent heatwave. She also commended
  Manager Beltran and Senior Center staff for their wonderful work.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Rodriguez asked whether bingo fundraisers could be
RODRIGUEZ  held, to which Manager Beltran indicated that staff will look into holding
  one sometime next year.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Gonzales asked about signing up for Mr. Sac classes, to
GONZALES  which Manager Beltran elaborated on the process.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Rodriguez spoke very highly of the field trip to Aquarium
RODRIGUEZ  of the Pacific as well as the luau held recently by the Recreation
  Department.

CHAIR DIAZ  Chair Diaz thanked the City Council, as well as staff in the Recreation
  and Police Departments for the recent 4th of July celebration. She
  especially appreciated that the events were split amongst two days.

PUBLIC SERVICES
DIRECTOR UPDATE  Director Rodriguez provided the following update:

  1) The Senior Center will be closed on September 5 in recognition of
  the Labor Day holiday.
  2) The proposed new hours for the Senior Center will be presented to
  the Council for its consideration at this Wednesday’s meeting. If
  approved, the new hours will begin on August 29.
